rationale: The literature partly supports the hypothesis that loss-of-function variants lead to haploinsufficiency and that missense variants cluster within specific domains (notably the catalytic JmjC and zinc-finger CxxC domains) where functional confirmation via DNA episignatures or in vitro assays is essential. However, the hypothesis claims that missense variants in these domains show 'overlapping severity' with haploinsufficiency. Multiple recent studies contradict this: missense variants in the CxxC zinc finger domain produce a distinct, more severe and clinically extensive neurodevelopmental syndrome with high penetrance, specific facial gestalt, and a unique episignature, whereas loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants exhibit incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.

evidence.text: In a combined cohort of 68 individuals (47 classified as carrying pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants), authors revealed a highly penetrant CxxC-domain-related phenotype with distinct facial features. Conversely, loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants showed variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance, complicating clinical interpretation and genetic counseling.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: We observe a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features supported by GestaltMatcher. In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling.

evidence.text: Characterization of 19 individuals with CxxC domain variants demonstrated that the core phenotype is more extensive than that seen in KDM2B haploinsufficiency. CxxC variants preserve mutant protein expression while significantly impairing DNA binding, causing a distinct syndrome possibly distinct from haploinsufficiency, with congenital heart defects present in up to 78% of individuals.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: The core phenotype of the KDM2B-CxxC cohort is more extensive as compared to that of individuals with KDM2B haploinsufficiency. All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay... Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals... This study shows that KDM2B CxxC variants cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome, possibly through a molecular mechanism different from haploinsufficiency.

evidence.text: Evaluation of 27 individuals confirmed 21 with (likely) pathogenic heterozygous KDM2B variants, establishing the CxxC domain as a mutational hotspot. Both loss-of-function variants and CxxC missense variants show specific, distinct episignatures, supporting functional divergence between variant classes.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated epigenetic signature
source.quote: We present evidence, including a shared epigenetic signature, to support a pathogenic classification of 15 KDM2B variants and identify the CxxC domain as a mutational hotspot. Both loss-of-function and CxxC-domain missense variants present with a specific subepisignature.

evidence.text: Three children with heterozygous CxxC domain variants presented with recurrent developmental delay, cardiac defects (atrial/ventricular septal defects), feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism, with targeted episignature profiling confirming diagnostic pathogenicity.

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Variants in KDM2B that primarily affect the CxxC DNA-binding domain are strongly linked to a specific epigenetic signature. We present three children with KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder, each with a heterozygous variant in the CxxC domain of KDM2B.

evidence.text: Screening of 706 families with developmental eye disorders identified two individuals with KDM2B CxxC variants causing characteristic DNA episignatures and severe complex structural eye defects accompanied by variable cardiac and renal anomalies.

source.title: Variants in the CxxC domain of the epigenetic regulator KDM2B support its role in developmental eye anomalies
source.quote: By screening 706 families with developmental eye disorders, we identified two cases with KDM2B-CxxC variants... both resulting in a characteristic KDM2B DNA episignature. Both individuals exhibited complex structural eye defects, with neurodevelopmental, cardiac and renal anomalies variably present.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits that missense variants in catalytic/zinc-finger domains show 'overlapping severity' with loss-of-function variants, whereas van Oirsouw et al. (2025, 2026) report that CxxC zinc finger missense variants cause a distinctly more extensive, highly penetrant phenotype compared to the incomplete penetrance and milder/variable expressivity of haploinsufficiency and JmjC domain variants.

The hypothesis assumes a unified haploinsufficiency mechanism across variants, whereas functional data demonstrate that CxxC variants preserve protein expression but impair DNA-binding, pointing to a distinct (dominant-negative or neomorphic/altered chromatin binding) disease mechanism rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Does mutant KDM2B protein harboring CxxC missense mutations exert a dominant-negative effect on non-canonical Polycomb Repressive Complex 1.1 (PRC1.1) recruitment relative to true null/haploinsufficient alleles?
new_directions.rationale: CxxC variants yield a distinct DNA methylation subepisignature and a significantly more penetrant, severe syndromic presentation than truncating alleles, suggesting altered complex assembly or competitive chromatin displacement rather than simple loss of one copy.

new_directions.question_text: What are the molecular and clinical differences between missense variants strictly in the JmjC catalytic domain versus the CxxC zinc finger domain?
new_directions.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. (2026) grouped JmjC missense variants together with loss-of-function variants in showing incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity, whereas CxxC variants show high penetrance, suggesting the catalytic and DNA-binding domains dictate markedly different clinical trajectories.
